newsitem.title: USA: Fahnestock agrees to stay in NYC in 16-year pact.
newsitem.headline: Fahnestock agrees to stay in NYC in 16-year pact.

text.p: New York State and City officials said Tuesday a Manhattan-based brokerage, Fahnestock, chose to stay in the city and turned down Secaucus, N.J., despite the big benefits it offered.

New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, who says his ability to keep employers from moving out of town shows how his Administration has turned New York City around, estimated the city would recoup its contribution in just over two weeks.

"Fahnestock's decision to remain and grow in New York City and the agreement we reached with the company are testament to the improved business environment in the city," Giuliani said, in a prepared statement. He estimated one-third of the city's contribution was linked to job creation.

Publishers McGraw-Hill and CPA firm Price Waterhouse LLP also recently agreed to stay in the city. The Giuliani Administration estimated it has kept 28 major companies, retaining 61,852 jobs and a projected 23,560 new positions over the next 10 to 20 years.
Gov. George Pataki said, "This is another vote of confidence by yet another financial industry firm that New York is -- and always will be -- the financial capital of the world," in prepared remarks.

The mayor said Fahnestock now pays the city $8.7 million in taxes a year. for the city. In return for agreeing to stay, the brokerage will get up to about $500,000 in sales tax exemptions and an estimated $400,000 of energy discounts if it keeps its present 398-employee workforce. Should the firm cut employees, however, the pact obliges it to repay or get reduced benefits.

Fahnestock also pledged to create another 125 jobs, and if it does, the firm gets a maximum of $250,000 more sales tax exemptions. This promise qualifies it for a $350,000 interest rate subsidy grant from the Empire State Development Corp, along with a $90,000 training grant.

"Fahnestock's U.S. headquarters have been located in New York City for over 100 years, and I am extremely pleased that this agreement will enable ys to stay and grow here," said Albert Lowenthal, the company chairman, in prepared remarks. The brokerage will move from its offices at 110 Wall Streat and lease 69,000 square feet at 125 Broad Street.
